subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Climate Engineering: Hacking the Planet's Thermostat
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Climate Engineering: Hacking the Planet's Thermostat.

hook.text: Stratospheric aerosol injection would spray sulfate particles into the upper atmosphere to reflect sunlight and cool the Earth.

buildup.text: Pinatubo's 1991 eruption ejected millions of tons of sulfur dioxide. Global temperatures dropped 0.5 degrees C for two years.

discovery.text: Scientists propose mimicking this artificially. High-altitude aircraft could spray aerosols continuously at relatively low cost.

twist.text: Once started, stopping abruptly could cause rapid warming — termination shock. The commitment would be ongoing for centuries.

climax.text: No international governance exists for geoengineering. Any country could deploy it unilaterally, affecting the entire planet.

punchline.text: Cool the planet with particles. Can't stop once you start. No one governs it.

quiz.question: What is termination shock in the context of climate engineering?
options: The sudden failure of aerosol spraying equipment at high altitudes
Rapid warming that would occur if aerosol injection were stopped abruptly
The psychological impact on populations learning they depend on geoengineering
